summary.headline: Go Digit Q2 FY27 CISR combined ratio rose to 99.8% from 94.9%, driven by Rs 63 crore Gujarat flood losses; ex-flood it was 97.4%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 on Indian Accounting Standards for the first time, with comparatives restated. Insurance revenue rose to Rs 2,720 crore from Rs 2,675 crore, and PAT excluding mark-to-market was Rs 208 crore versus Rs 277 crore a year earlier. Excluding flood losses, PAT was Rs 255 crore, up sequentially from Rs 239 crore in Q1. GDPI fell 1.2% against industry growth of 7%, with private car standalone own damage premium down 40% after April-May price corrections. Management said private car own damage attritional loss ratio improved from 85.3% in Q1 to 81.1% in Q2.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Motor premium fell 4.1%, driven by private car down 10.7% and standalone own damage premium down 40%. Two-wheeler grew 18.6% and commercial vehicles fell 20%; school bus and auto-rickshaw writing was cut on weak commissions. Motor market share was 5.68% in Q2 vs 5.58% in Q1; own damage share was 4.99% vs 4.76%.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Fire gross written premium fell 29.9%. Gross earned loss ratio was 59% in Q2 (61.5% for H1) after flood losses, with engineering at 62.4% and liability at 25.7% in Q2.

segments.name: Health, travel and PA
segments.commentary: Retail health is under 6-7% of the book; the rest is group health. Group health growth was held back by Rs 95 crore of government and health reinsurance premium not renewed. Management estimates employer-employee business at about 80% of the health and PA book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Equity and REIT/InvIT allocation is 9.6% of AUM on book value, excluding AT1 bonds, with unrealised equity gains of about Rs 148 crore. Duration was 4.8 years in September and 4.9 in October, against 5.2 in March 2025. Fixed-income reinvestment yield was about 8% in October, and overall yield is about 7.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management is not giving formal guidance; it said Q3 will show how the festive-season month-on-month trend develops.
Management expects growth declines to keep reducing, with pricing discipline returning in fire from mid-September.
Equity allocation may move toward 12.5% of AUM including REITs, subject to the capital allocation model.
Duration may be extended back toward 5.2 years depending on interest rates.
The company will hold an analyst day in February covering Indian Accounting Standards in more detail.
Management said the Indian Accounting Standards transition for the whole industry takes effect from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Private car own damage attritional loss ratio fell to 81.1% in Q2 from 85.3% in Q1; the reported Q2 loss ratio was 93% including floods.
The commercial lines product has been launched with a full pricing and rating model; quotes are currently below 20 and management will wait about six months before judging scale.
Long-term advance premium was Rs 3,556 crore at 30 September 2026.
Solvency is 2.40x, with additional net worth of about Rs 3,300 crore that management said cannot currently be distributed or used to write business.
demand_pricing: No TP price hikes yet; the market is soft except property, where rates have firmed since mid-September.
Industry GDPI grew 7% while Digit's GDPI fell 1.2%; GWP fell 3.6%, or was flat excluding health reinsurance inward and government health.
Management attributes the higher expense ratio mainly to a rising two-wheeler mix, where commissions are higher, and says operational expenses are among the industry's best.
Management said it had lost TP market share this year and would not match commission levels it considers uneconomic.
Group health employer-employee loss ratios are above 100% for the industry, according to management, and it wants a 5% group health price increase.

qa_highlights.question: How will the distribution paper (EoM and commission changes) affect TP profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discussion paper acknowledges that the current EoM guidelines have not produced the intended outcome. It declined to speculate on final guidance and suggested analysts run their own models using the commission and opex split on the website.

qa_highlights.question: What are the loss ratios without discounting, and what discount rate was used?
qa_highlights.answer: Discounting affects about 20% of TP outstanding claims plus IBNR. The risk-free rate is set at each quarter end plus 25% of the gap to the AAA yield as illiquidity premium; September discount rates were about 6.2-6.6% for liabilities up to one year and about 7.5% beyond eight years. Management declined to publish a non-discounted combined ratio, citing the Rs 171 crore finance expense offset.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the expense ratio rise in a soft market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the growing two-wheeler mix, which carries higher commissions than other lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will Digit compete if commissions and TP pricing are fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commission and price are the only two levers and it will write business only where commissions are economic. It added that distribution will rely on existing partners and new channels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share of Gujarat flood losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its fire loss share is likely below its market share, and that motor is hard to judge because of EV battery write-offs and salvage values. Flood losses were Rs 63 crore net, against Rs 10 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is health loss ratio improving, and what is the group employer-employee mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said group health loss ratios are broadly unchanged. It estimated employer-employee at about 80% of health and PA, with retail around 6%. It cited a 5% group health price rise as enough to support growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IDBI Bank transaction's potential impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no information beyond Fairfax's announcement that it will sell its Digit stake to IDBI Bank. It said a bancassurance tie-up would be welcome if the bank became a corporate agent, since bancassurance is typically more profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Which products carry the onerous contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said onerous contracts arise in motor TP and group health; testing is done at a granular line-of-business level with the auditors.

risks_watch: Flood losses and the Gujarat catastrophe event, along with the reinsurance recoveries that follow, drive quarterly CISR volatility.
Discussion paper on EoM and commission could change TP and group health economics.
Persistent group health losses and government health business pricing in the industry.
Continued degrowth in private car and fire premium, and whether festive-season trends improve in Q3.
Discount-rate and illiquidity premium sensitivity to spreads, which management said will reverse in the following quarter.
Possible IDBI Bank bancassurance tie-up, which depends on the Fairfax-Government of India transaction.
Possible shift to IFRS-style reporting, and the ongoing debate over the lack of a non-discounted combined ratio.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the underlying numbers and the private car own damage turn, but defensive on accounting comparability; management declined to provide a non-discounted combined ratio or onerous contract detail and deferred those to February.
key_quotes: And overall, we continue to choose profitability over growth, and we continue to hold that choice as we speak.
So basically, I think our onerous contract is coming from motor TP and group health.
I think quarter two is showing us that it is maybe better than stabilizing because I give the exact numbers.
